commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][KV Offload] Use private pinned tensors for CPU KV offload
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Native CPU KV offload stalled during startup on an 8x MI308X node with TP8 and a 500 GiB offload pool. Six ranks reported `cudaHostRegister failed (code=1)`, and the engine never became ready.

`_uses_shared_region()` includes ROCm through `is_cuda_alike()`, so each worker registers the entire shared mmap region. Exclude ROCm to use the existing private per-rank pinned tensor allocator instead. The CUDA path is unchanged; ROCm no longer uses shared-region replicated KV deduplication.

Unlike #51081 (chunked registration) and #52296 (coordinated registration), this change bypasses shared mmap allocation on ROCm.

## Test Plan

Tested with vLLM 0.29.0 and ROCm 7.2.3 on two 8x MI308X hosts, running GLM-5.3 with TP8, FP8 E4M3 KV cache, and:

    --kv-offloading-size 500 --kv-offloading-backend native

Check startup and generation, then evict a cached 32K prompt from GPU KV cache using distinct filler prompts and replay it.

## Test Result

- Both hosts completed startup and served generation requests.
- Transfer counters confirmed CPU-to-GPU KV reload after eviction.
- The tested 32K gold-answer prompt returned the expected answer on both the cold request and the post-eviction replay.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][DSv4.1] Preserve NaN-scored candidate block indices
commits.pr_body:
DeepSeek-V4.1 TP4 MegaAttention can fail startup with a DeepGEMM sparse-slot assertion during dummy prefill/autotuning. The candidate-source logits contain NaNs. Although `torch.topk` selects their block IDs, `value > -inf` discards them, leaving only the pinned newest block. Expanding that underfilled row repeats its last block inside the prefix DeepGEMM expects to be unique (389 copies of block 388 in the captured failing rows).

Exclude only the `-inf` padding sentinel when storing selected candidates. This retains NaN-scored block IDs, keeps the active prefix unique for the observed configuration, and works with the existing DeepGEMM dependency. Finite-score selection is unchanged; this adds no kernel, buffer, fallback, or host synchronization. It does not sanitize logits or fix the upstream numerical source of dummy-run NaNs.

Extend the existing candidate suite with empty/partial rows and aligned/unaligned starts under zero/NaN scores, and update its reference to retain selected NaN entries.

Validation on GB200:

- Both new NaN regression cases fail against the original selector; both finite control cases pass.
- All 13 candidate tests pass on PR commit `707b81b021`; scoped pre-commit hooks (including mypy) pass.
- Four captured TP-rank inputs replay through unmodified DeepGEMM after the fix, recovering 389 unique blocks in each previously failing row.
- Selector checks at 8K, 50K and 100K cover random, zero, NaN and mixed-NaN scores; finite outputs match the original exactly.
- The identical selector change on the previously validated model worktree passes real-weight TP4 MegaAttention startup with sparse logits, DSpark5, autotuning and FULL target/draft graphs. Short (18-token) and long (16,526-token) chat prompts both return the expected answer `4`. This is a serving smoke, not a full accuracy evaluation or a full-model build of current main. No full accuracy evaluation was repeated.

Duplicate-work check: #56558 optimizes the candidate-source selector but explicitly preserves NaN exclusion. #50201 and #49897 address the downstream token top-k kernel. None fixes this candidate-store predicate. vllm-project/DeepGEMM#16 instead adds repeated-index support to the native metadata API; this PR prevents vLLM from constructing the invalid active prefix for the observed NaN case and needs no dependency update. No linked issue.

AI assistance: implementation, investigation and validation used OpenAI Codex. The human submitter confirmed reviewing every changed line of commit `707b81b021` and running the relevant GPU tests.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] DiffusionGemma: hand out stashed logprobs only on the committing step
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Two concurrent DiffusionGemma requests with `logprobs` on can stomp on each other's logprobs, one then fails with an HTTP 500.

The diffusion sampler stashes a request's top-k logprobs on the step it converges and attaches them to the SamplerOutput on the commit step. The attach loop pops the stash for every decoding request in the batch though, not just the ones committing on this step. 

So... if request B converges in the same step that request A commits, B's logprobs get emitted under A. When B's own commit comes around there is nothing left to pop, the API sees fewer logprobs than tokens, and chat completions dies with `IndexError: list index out of range in _create_chat_logprobs`.

Any two requests whose schedules line up one step apart will hit this, so it shows up as soon as you run a concurrency sweep with logprobs. The fix is to only pop for the slots that are actually committing this step.

This is split out of #57250 since it's a standalone bug.

## Test plan

Run the serve command with --max-logprobs 32 and a 2-way to 32-way sweep of identical requests with logprobs on.

Hardware: 1 DGX Spark.

Before: identical requests sent together line up one step apart, so a 2-way sweep already fails with 500 `list index out of range` on the request that converged while 
the other committed.

After: 32-way sweep is clean, every response carries one logprob entry per token, and the 1-way path is unchanged.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend][Core] Add release_kv_cache_memory() API
commits.pr_body:
## Motivation

Sleep level 2 releases KV cache memory, but it also discards model weights. This
is unnecessarily expensive when a framework only needs temporary GPU headroom
while keeping the same model instance resident.

One concrete use case is model weight update in RL training. The workaround in
[verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) uses
`sleep(level=2)` followed by `wake_up(tags=["weights"])` before updating the
standalone model. Releasing only the KV cache reduces peak GPU memory and can
avoid OOM during the update, without discarding and remapping weights.

## Summary

This PR adds `release_kv_cache_memory()` as a dedicated KV-only partial-sleep
operation. It discards KV cache allocations, keeps model weights resident, and
pauses scheduling until the released memory is restored with the existing
`wake_up()` API.

## Implementation

### Call flow

The offline and server entry points converge on the same engine path:

```text
LLM.release_kv_cache_memory() -> LLMEngine ---------\
                                                       -> EngineCore
POST /release_kv_cache_memory -> EngineClient ------/       |
                                                             v
                                      Executor.discard(("kv_cache",))
                                                             |
                                                             v
                                               Worker -> SleepModeBackend
                                                             |
                                                             v
                                           CuMem/XPU allocator.discard(tags)
```

`EngineCore` first pauses the scheduler and clears the prefix cache. Depending
on the selected pause mode, it either handles existing requests immediately or
waits for in-flight requests to finish before asking all workers to discard KV
cache allocations. The scheduler remains paused after release; a discard
failure also fails closed instead of resuming scheduling with potentially
partially unmapped memory.

At allocator level, only mapped allocations tagged `kv_cache` are unmapped and
released, without a CPU backup. Per-allocation mapping state prevents duplicate
unmap or map operations when release, sleep, and wake-up calls are mixed.

### Interaction with sleep levels

`release_kv_cache_memory()` is treated as a KV-only partial sleep. A later
`sleep(1)` or `sleep(2)` can upgrade that state to a full sleep:

| Current state | Operation | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fully awake | `release_kv_cache_memory()` | KV cache discarded, weights resident, scheduler paused |
| KV-only sleeping | `sleep(1)` | Weights offloaded, KV cache remains discarded |
| KV-only sleeping | `sleep(2)` | Weights discarded, KV cache remains discarded |
| KV-only sleeping | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | KV cache remapped and scheduling resumed |
| Full sleep | `wake_up(["kv_cache"])` | Only KV cache remapped; weights remain sleeping and scheduling stays paused |
| Full sleep | `wake_up()` | All allocations restored and scheduling resumed |

The executor tracks the exact internal state with `sleeping_tags`. Scheduling
is resumed only after no sleeping tags remain.

### Logging and observability

This PR reuses the existing sleep-state logger instead of adding a dedicated
`kv_cache_released` Prometheus state. After KV release, the existing metrics
report `awake=0`, `weights_offloaded=0`, and `discard_all=0`: the engine is not
available for scheduling, but it is not in sleep level 1 or 2. The precise
resource state remains available internally through `sleeping_tags`.

There is currently no requirement to monitor KV-only release separately. If
that becomes useful, a dedicated Prometheus state and its transition logic can
be added in a follow-up change.

## Scope

The public API intentionally supports only KV cache release. Existing sleep
levels already cover the other current cases:

- `sleep(1)` offloads weights and discards KV cache memory.
- `sleep(2)` discards all managed GPU memory.

A generic public tag API would also need to define whether each tag is discarded
or offloaded, increasing the API surface and overlapping with existing sleep
semantics. More fine-grained public memory management can be discussed when a
concrete additional use case appears; the internal `discard(tags)` path remains
extensible.

## Related work

- [vLLM#42658](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42658) explores generic
  tag-level sleep management. This PR instead provides a smaller, explicit
  end-to-end API for the known KV-only use case.
- [vLLM#46438](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46438) contains related
  allocator-level selective-discard work.
- [verl#7373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/7373) demonstrates the
  downstream model-update use case and its current sleep/wake workaround.

This PR does not duplicate the generic public API proposed in #42658; its scope
and semantics are intentionally narrower.

## Tests

Local validation used an Enroot container on one NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3
and Torch 2.13.0+cu130. The PR Python source was tested with the image's
precompiled native libraries (vLLM distribution 0.1.dev20073+g8e685d198).

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py \
  -k "kv_cache_release_rejects_unsafe_state or pause_synchronizes_device" \
  -v -o addopts=""
```

Result: **5 passed**. Rejection coverage checks an unpaused scheduler, pending
requests, and pending batches independently, with no cache reset or discard on
failure. Removing each guard in memory caused its corresponding test to fail.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py \
  -k release_kv_cache_memory_preserves_generation \
  -x -v -o addopts="" --timeout=600
```

Result: **2 passed**. Real Qwen3-0.6B generation covers rejection without a pause,
KV-only release/wake-up, and release followed by full level-1 sleep/wake-up.
Checks use process-local mapped memory and compare greedy token IDs before and
after restoration.

```bash
pre-commit run --files tests/basic_correctness/test_mem.py tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py
```

Result: all applicable hooks passed.

The test revision changes no production behavior; no additional model
benchmark was run beyond the generation-equivalence checks above.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to review the implementation, revise and validate the tests,
and draft this description.
The submitter reviewed the resulting changes and test scope.

commits.pr_title: [AMD][Bugfix] Make the nested-RoPE patch reach automatic validation
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Two spec-decode checkpoints fail to load at the same line, for two unrelated reasons:

```
AttributeError: 'float' object has no attribute 'get'    # poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'      # deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7
  transformers/modeling_rope_utils.py:850, in validate_rope
```

`validate_rope` treats a `rope_parameters` mapping as nested whenever the config declares `layer_types` and any top-level key appears in it, then iterates **all** of the mapping's values, guarding only against `None`. Any non-dict entry next to the per-layer dicts therefore raises, and the reported type is just whichever stray the iterator reaches first.

**Two producers, and only one is a malformed config.**

- `deepseek-ai/dspark_gemma4_12b_block7` ships the strays itself: its `config.json` stores `"rope_type": "default"` and `"rope_theta": null` beside the `full_attention` / `sliding_attention` dicts. `Gemma4TextConfig` overrides `convert_rope_params_to_dict` with a bare `return kwargs` — one of six config classes in transformers 5.17 that do (`DiffusionGemmaTextConfig`, `Gemma4TextConfig`, `Gemma4UnifiedTextConfig`, `LagunaConfig`, `MellumConfig`, `MiMoV2FlashConfig`) — so neither it nor `standardize_rope_params` ever runs to normalize them.
- `poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1-NVFP4`'s checkpoint is clean: its `rope_parameters` holds only the two per-layer dicts. The stray is injected at load time. The repo ships remote code (`auto_map` → `configuration_laguna.LagunaConfig`, under `trust_remote_code=True`) which inherits the base `convert_rope_params_to_dict`, and that does a flat `rope_parameters.setdefault("rope_theta", ...)` without checking for the nested shape; `standardize_rope_params` Case 2 then only walks `set(layer_types)`, so it never removes it again.

**The existing workaround does not run on the path that needs it.** `huggingface_hub`'s `@strict` decorator snapshots every `validate_*` method into `__class_validators__` at class creation, and automatic post-`__init__` validation dispatches off that snapshot rather than off the class attribute. Assigning `PretrainedConfig.validate_rope` therefore only affects explicit `config.validate_rope()` calls — which is why `laguna` fails today *even though its `model_type` is already in the allowlist*. That list is not unique to `PreTrainedConfig` either: transformers decorates individual config classes with `@strict` and each owns a separate snapshot.

## Changes

- Add `_install_hf_config_validator`, which sets the class attribute and then walks the loaded `PretrainedConfig` subclass tree, rewriting each `__class_validators__` snapshot that still holds the superseded function. Matching is by **identity**, so a genuine per-model override such as `DeepseekV4Config.validate_rope` is left in place. Classes imported later snapshot the patched function themselves.
- Route **both** rope patches through it. Routing the `sarvam_mla` shim is load-bearing rather than tidiness: if it keeps the plain assignment, a later nested-rope patch supersedes a function that is in no snapshot and the rewrite silently has no effect.
- Add `gemma4_text` to `_PATCH_HF_NESTED_ROPE_VALIDATION`. Per review, the patch stays gated on `model_type` rather than installing for every model, so malformed checkpoint configs are not silently accommodated. The subclass walk is what makes the gate sufficient: it repairs an already-frozen snapshot, so it no longer matters whether the patch installs during the target's parse or the draft's.

Four hunks in one file. The warning, the removal predicate, the wrapper signature and the existing docstrings are unchanged.

**No tests are added.** The two reproducers are GPU e2e suites; I did not add unit coverage for `_install_hf_config_validator` (the snapshot rewrite and the identity-match carve-out). Happy to add it in `tests/test_config.py` next to the regression #57189 introduced, if reviewers want it.

## Testing

Run on MI355X in `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-af1c01499b289be555c475669ba50a88e96d846e`, with this branch's Python source overlaid on the image's compiled extensions. Caveat: that image is 125 commits behind this branch's base and predates the transformers 5.17.0 bump (#56108), so the kernels are older than the Python. The image ships `transformers==5.17.0` / `huggingface_hub==1.31.0`, the transformers minor that introduced the crash. Each test ran in its own pytest session, matching how CI shards them.

```bash
python3 -m pytest -v -s -rA tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dspark/test_dspark.py -k gemma4-deepspec --no-header
python3 -m pytest -v -s -rA tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py -k laguna-nvfp4-mrv2 --no-header
python3 -m pytest tests/test_config.py -q --no-header
```

| | `main` (fef55fd26d) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `test_dspark_...[gemma4-deepspec]` | **FAILED** — `'str' object has no attribute 'get'` | **PASSED** — accuracy 0.930, acceptance rate 0.567, acceptance length 4.971 (floors 0.874 / 0.551 / 4.750) |
| `test_dflash_correctness[laguna-nvfp4-mrv2]` | **FAILED** — `'float' object has no attribute 'get'` | GSM8K eval runs end to end; **fails the acceptance assertion**, `3.051 < 3.195`, accuracy 0.895 |
| `tests/test_config.py` | 2 failed, 371 passed, 6 skipped | 2 failed, 371 passed, 6 skipped |

The `test_config.py` failures are identical on both sides and pre-existing — `test_rope_customization` and `test_eagle_draft_model_config` need gated HF repos and the container has no token. Also checked: a non-allowlisted model with a flat `rope_parameters` is left untouched, and the `sarvam_mla` legacy `validate_rope(ignore_keys=...)` path still works.

**The bug is not ROCm-specific.** Reproduced on an **NVIDIA GB300** (`vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-0bfc7a15d0...`, same transformers 5.17.0, native NVFP4 via `FlashInferCuteDslNvFp4LinearKernel` + `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM` MoE): the same `Dropping ['rope_theta'] from rope_parameters` fires and both Laguna configs resolve, so unpatched CUDA fails the same way AMD does.

**On the laguna result, stated plainly: this change does not turn that test green.** It turns a config-parse crash into an assertion failure — the GSM8K eval now runs end to end, which it never did before, and the test then fails the acceptance-length threshold. That shortfall is not caused by this change, and it is not AMD-specific:

| hardware | NVFP4 path | acceptance_len | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| MI355X | emulation | 3.051 | 0.895 |
| GB300 | native | **3.0495** | 0.890 |
| enforced floor | | **3.195** (`3.55 × 0.9`) | 0.700 |

Two vendors, native versus emulated quantization, agreeing to three significant figures, ~14% under the reference. In-run metrics oscillate 2.97 / 3.09 / 3.04, so ~3.05 is steady state rather than a tail artifact. The `3.55` figure is annotated in the sibling references as coming from Table 1 of the DFlash paper rather than a measured run, and this parametrization has never completed in CI — it has crashed at config parse since it was added in #50330 — so nothing has ever checked it. I have not found a prior run of it on any hardware to compare against. Worth fixing platform-agnostically in a separate PR rather than with a per-platform carve-out; if anyone has an H200 nightly result for it, that would settle it.

Note these two suites are `optional: true` nightlies (`:nvidia: (H200 MIG 35GB) Spec Decode AL DFlash/DSpark Nightly`, with `:amd: (MI300)` mirrors) whose `source_file_dependencies` do not include `vllm/transformers_utils/config.py` — so this PR does not trigger either job, and no CI number is coming without a manual run.

`ruff check` and `ruff format` pass at the pinned v0.14.0. The diff touches configuration parsing only, but the patch deletes keys from `rope_parameters` before validation for the two gated model types, so it is not output-neutral by construction. Evals run: the two acceptance-rate tests above. Not run: the other four parametrizations in these shards.

## Notes

Related to #57188, which the merged #57189 already fixed and closed — that layer-type gate is on `main` and this change leaves it byte-identical. The gate is in fact what makes the patch safe for flat mappings; it does not address either failure here. #57193 was a duplicate of #57189 and was closed unmerged.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Restore KV cache metadata GET method for external event consumer
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`get_kv_cache_group_metadata` is deleted by https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53941 as dead code but is actually used by external event consumers like Dynamo. The PR brings the function call back.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Add record_logical_topk_ready to ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl (GLM-5.3-Flash boot crash)
commits.pr_body:
## Why this is not duplicating #56604

#56604 (open since 2026-09-12) fixes the same crash class by adding a **default no-op `record_logical_topk_ready` on the `MLAAttentionImpl` base class** in `vllm/v1/attention/backend.py`, so every backend silently inherits it.

This PR instead adds the method **on `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` itself**, mirroring the existing `SparseMLACommonImpl` contract (`vllm/model_executor/layers/attention/sparse_mla_attention.py:717`): impls that participate in sparse-MLA index groups implement the hook with real semantics; impls that don't declare an explicit no-op at their own site.

Trade-off: the base-class default in #56604 is broader (also covers any other backend that skips `SparseMLACommonImpl`) but weakens the interface — a new sparse backend that *should* implement index-group notification would silently no-op instead of failing loudly. This PR keeps that failure loud and fixes the one backend that currently crashes (ROCm AITER sparse MLA, GLM-5.3-Flash on MI350X). Either fix resolves the boot regression in #57248; happy to withdraw this in favor of #56604 if maintainers prefer the base-class default.

## Description

`MLAAttention.forward` calls `impl.record_logical_topk_ready()` on every sparse layer (`vllm/model_executor/layers/mla.py:235`). `ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl` inherits `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` directly (not `SparseMLACommonImpl`) and never gained the method, so serving GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (gfx950, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE`) crashes at the first forward with `AttributeError: 'ROCMAiterMLASparseImpl' object has no attribute 'record_logical_topk_ready'`.

This impl shares the top-k indices buffer via `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` but does not participate in `SparseMLAIndexGroup` host-side prefetching, so the correct implementation is a no-op.

Fixes the first boot regression in #57248.

## Test commands run and results

- Reproduced on the cluster before the fix: nightly `af1c01499` on 8×MI350X TP8, engine dies at first forward with the AttributeError above.
- With the equivalent no-op method patched in-pod (same 5-line change), the model boots and serves; combined with `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0` it passes the full chunked-prefill repro suite with zero faults (details in #57227).
- `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` — syntax OK; AST check confirms the method is now on the class.
- No GPU/ROCm environment is available in CI for the full path, so no new automated test is added here; #56604 already adds an interface-level test (`tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_topk_ready_hook.py`) that covers this method's presence on backends.

## AI assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance (Hermes Agent). The change was reviewed and validated end-to-end on the affected hardware by the submitter: the same no-op patch was applied in-pod on the MI350X cluster and confirmed to resolve the crash.

DSpark's non-causal draft window has 133 valid keys at draft length 5, padded to 256 indices. The DSV4.1 FlashInfer integration passed the padded width as the active sparse length, so padding entered softmax normalization. A constant-value reference expecting 1 returned 0.51953125 (133/256). Short contexts also inherited causal visibility from the launcher's per-request query positions.

Use the valid SWA length, retaining FlashInfer's required 128-column minimum, and present each draft query with the full non-causal sequence length. Prepare the per-token active lengths and sequence lengths once in the metadata builder, using persistent buffers refreshed before FULL CUDA graph replay and shared across layers. Singleton query/output views remove the need to construct query offsets in each layer. This changes vLLM metadata only; no FlashInfer source changes or new Triton kernel are needed. The two int32 buffers use 8 bytes per configured maximum batched token per builder (64 KiB at capacity 8192).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Reject stop strings on --tokens-only servers instead of silently ignoring them
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Partially addresses #57052 (the `--tokens-only` half; the derender-side stop-string truncation is a separate design discussion tracked there).

A `--tokens-only` server sets `sampling_params.detokenize = False` **after** the request has already passed validation, bypassing the `SamplingParams` guard that forbids `stop` strings without detokenization. Downstream, the tokenizer-less `IncrementalDetokenizer` never calls `check_stop_strings`, so client `stop` strings were **silently ignored** — generation ran to EOS or `max_tokens` with no error, warning, or log line. The failure is easy to miss because `stop_token_ids` still work (they need no detokenization).

This PR rejects the combination with a 400 in `serve_tokens`, mirroring the error a client already gets when it sets `detokenize=False` itself (see the first leg of the existing `test_stop_string_workflow`). The error message points at the documented contract from that same test: check stop strings on the coordinator, or use `stop_token_ids`.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Checked open PRs before submitting (`gh pr list --search` on "stop", "tokens-only", "include_stop_str_in_output", "derender", plus `57052 in:body`). The closest is #46310, which rejects `stop` when `--skip-tokenizer-init` is set — but that guards `SamplingParams` construction from CLI-level config and does not catch this path, where the request validates cleanly (client-side `detokenize` defaults to `True`) and `force_no_detokenize` flips it afterwards. No open PR touches the scale-out `serve_tokens` validation.

## Test Plan

New test `test_stop_strings_rejected_when_tokens_only` in the existing `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py`, using the file's indirect server parametrization to launch with `--tokens-only`: asserts `stop` → 400 with a "stop strings" error message, and that the identical request with `stop": null` succeeds on the same server.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_stop_strings_rejected_when_tokens_only -v
# regression on the default (non --tokens-only) server:
.venv/bin/python -m pytest "tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_generate_endpoint" "tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py::test_stop_string_workflow" -v
pre-commit run --files vllm/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/serving.py tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py
```

## Test Result

All three tests pass locally (macOS CPU build, Qwen3-0.6B; the local runs added `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.25` to the server fixture args purely to fit local RAM — the committed test keeps the standard args):

- `test_stop_strings_rejected_when_tokens_only`: **1 passed**
- `test_generate_endpoint`, `test_stop_string_workflow` (default server, guard must not fire): **2 passed**
- `pre-commit run --files ...` (including `mypy-3.10`): all hooks pass

No model evaluation needed: the change is request validation only; accepted requests produce byte-identical output.

---

AI assistance (Claude) was used for the investigation and drafting; the change and test runs were reviewed and driven by the human submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Add fused DFlash2 grouped convolution
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- Fuse DFlash2's grouped dynamic convolution in one Triton custom op, keeping the existing Torch CPU fallback. The kernel stays in `qwen3_dflash2.py`.
- Use row-aligned tiles: 1024 elements for at least 128 rows with hidden width divisible by 1024, otherwise 512. Four warps; no autotuner.
- Cover non-power-of-two dimensions, strided coefficient views, multiple tap counts, and both tile paths in FP32/BF16.
- Add real-checkpoint GSM8K accuracy and acceptance-length coverage to the existing H200 35 GB DFlash nightly job. Keep this case excluded from its AMD mirror; the Speculators/MTP job is unchanged.

The implementation docstring credits LightSeek TokenSpeed PR https://github.com/lightseekorg/tokenspeed/pull/1399.

## End-to-end validation

One NVIDIA B300, TP=1, V2 model runner, compilation and CUDA graphs enabled. Target: `nvidia/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4`; unchanged BF16 draft: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`. Full GSM8K: 1,319 questions, 5-shot chat, thinking disabled, temperature 0, max output 256 tokens, max model length 4,096, max batch 32, seven speculative tokens.

| Implementation | GSM8K accuracy | Mean acceptance length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original Torch convolution, NVFP4 target, run 1 | 92.0% | 6.14 |
| Original Torch convolution, NVFP4 target, repeat | 91.2% | 6.13 |
| Fused kernel before final tuning, NVFP4 target, run 1 | 91.1% | 6.13 |
| Fused kernel before final tuning, NVFP4 target, repeat | 92.2% | 6.14 |
| Final row-aligned kernel, NVFP4 target | **92.2%** | **6.14** |

All passed. Acceptance length is `1 + accepted_tokens / draft_steps`. Accuracy varies across runs; this is not an exact-output-equivalence claim. The compiled draft graph was inspected to confirm it invokes the convolution custom op. CI checks accuracy >= 90% and AL >= `6.14 * 0.95` (5.833).

The NVFP4 target reduces reported target-plus-draft model-load memory from 54.0 GiB to 22.85 GiB; this is not total serving/KV-cache memory. The case runs in the existing H200 35 GB DFlash nightly job, with its 90-minute timeout unchanged, and remains excluded from the AMD mirror. H200 has a Marlin weight-only fallback for the NVFP4 target. Local validation was on B300; H200 execution and memory fit remain unverified.

Earlier BF16-target validation also passed: original Torch convolution 92.2% / AL 6.19; initial fused kernel 92.0% / AL 6.19 in two runs. CI now uses the smaller NVFP4 checkpoint instead.

## Kernel performance

### Initial fusion versus Torch (before the final row-aligned tuning)

Actual checkpoint shape: hidden size 5,120, BF16, block size 8, group size 16, two taps, strided coefficients. B300, FlashInfer CUPTI timing, CUDA graphs, cold L2, four alternating-order trials; median latency. Baseline is the existing expression under `torch.compile`. Correctness checked before timing.

| Batch | Torch / Triton latency (us) | Torch / Triton effective GB/s | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 1.889 / 1.920 | 103 / 101 | 0.98x |
| 2 | 2.064 / 2.016 | 179 / 183 | 1.02x |
| 4 | 2.176 / 2.112 | 329 / 339 | 1.03x |
| 8 | 2.496 / 2.320 | 566 / 609 | 1.08x |
| 16 | 3.296 / 2.720 | 851 / 1,032 | 1.21x |
| 32 | 4.576 / 3.599 | 1,222 / 1,554 | 1.27x |

Effective bandwidth counts each input once and the output once: `2 * (2*rows*5120 + rows*2*320 + 2*5120)` bytes, `rows = batch*8`. These are kernel-only gains, not end-to-end speedups; batch 1 is approximately neutral.

### Final row-aligned tuning versus the posted fused kernel

Integrated confirmation on all 11 surveyed hidden-width/block-size pairs, at batches 1/32/256, BF16, group 16, two taps, strided coefficients. B300, CUPTI, CUDA graphs, cold L2, four alternating-order trials of 100 ms. Compared with posted commit `fd19503785`: batch 1 is effectively unchanged; batch 32 is 1.006–1.172x faster; batch 256 is 1.078–1.328x faster.

Representative batch-256 results (posted fused kernel → final tuned kernel):

| Hidden / block | Tile | Useful GB/s | Latency (us) | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2560 / 8 | 512 | 2649 → 2856 | 8.384 → 7.776 | 1.078x |
| 5120 / 8 | 1024 | 3038 → 3921 | 14.624 → 11.328 | 1.291x |
| 6656 / 16 | 512 | 3300 → 3610 | 35.057 → 32.049 | 1.094x |

Useful bytes = `2 * (2*rows*hidden + (2*rows-batch)*(hidden/16) + 2*hidden)`, excluding unused second-tap coefficients at block starts. This is an ideal useful-bandwidth estimate, not measured HBM traffic. These remain kernel-only speedups. Block-7/anchor/MoE entries in the shape sweep are kernel coverage, not full-model compatibility claims.

## Tests

All GPU workloads used `chg run -g=1 --`; no `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` overrides. Commands below assume the checkout's Python environment is activated (including its `bin` directory on PATH):

```bash
chg run -g=1 -- .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py -q
chg run -g=1 -- env VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py -k dflash2
pre-commit run --files .buildkite/test_areas/spec_decode.yaml tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/dflash/test_dflash.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash2.py vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash2.py
```

- Focused suite: **16 passed**, including the aligned 1024-tile path and non-aligned 512-tile fallback.
- Integrated scratch boundary sweep: **570/570 bitwise comparisons passed** against the posted kernel. Covers all 11 model shape pairs, FP32/FP16/BF16, empty/one-row inputs, strided inputs/coefficients, ragged rows/widths, 1/2/3 taps, log-scaled values, and 127/128/129-row boundaries.
- Full NVFP4 model test: **1 passed** for each of the five runs above, including the final tuned implementation (**226.52 s**, including startup). First NVFP4 runs took about 5.5 minutes due to compilation/autotuning; warm-cache runs took 3.5–3.7 minutes. The smaller checkpoint is not a claim of faster CI.
- Changed-file pre-commit: **passed**, including mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import and CUDA API checks. CI YAML parsing/selection checks passed.
- Local environment: PyTorch 2.13.0, Triton 3.7.1, Transformers 5.15.0, FlashInfer 0.6.17. Initial startup failed on both branches due to a missing generated FlashMLA Python module in the worktrees; linking the existing installed artifact fixed the environment without code changes. The first NVFP4 attempt on both branches also stopped before evaluation because `ninja` was missing from PATH; using the already-installed venv `bin` directory resolved it without dependency/code changes.

## Duplicate work

Rechecked open vLLM PRs for `dflash2 conv`, `fused grouped conv`, and DFlash2 GSM8K/acceptance coverage. No other open PR implements this kernel/dispatch or this CI case. The companion TP-reduction and packed-top-k PRs remain separate.

AI assistance was used to analyze the upstream implementation, implement the change, and write/run the tests and benchmarks. Human submitter review is required before merge.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Release stale FlashMLA workspace views after growth
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Release obsolete FlashMLA scratch storage when another layer grows the shared workspace.

`FlashMLASparseImpl` keeps constructor-time tensor views in `q_concat_buffer`, `prefill_bf16_workspace`, and, with PCP+DCP, `gathered_kv_workspace`. When `WorkspaceManager` grows its allocation, those views keep the old storage alive. Both buffers remain allocated, reducing the memory available for KV cache.

This change stores shapes and dtypes, reserves capacity during initialization, and reacquires simultaneous views from the current workspace when used. Workspace sizing, tensor layout, and the manager's locking policy remain unchanged.

### Observed impact

We reproduced this on GLM-5.3 with DP/EP64, TP1, MTP1, automatic KV/context sizing, and a 0.95 GPU memory target, using a vLLM 0.29.0-based deployment. Allocator snapshots showed a 5,904 MiB FlashMLA workspace retained alongside a new 6,144 MiB MoE workspace on 18 of 64 ranks. The new allocation was traced to `FusedMoEKernelModularImpl._allocate_buffers` during profiling.

The corresponding fix on that deployed version produced these startup measurements:

| Measurement | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ranks retaining both allocations | 18 | 0 |
| Minimum KV capacity per rank | 490,816 tokens | 603,904 tokens |
| Total KV capacity across 64 ranks | 36,934,975 tokens | 38,971,455 tokens |

Total allocated memory recovered was **103.78125 GiB**. These are startup allocation measurements, not throughput or model-accuracy results. This PR ports the fix to current upstream and also covers its PCP+DCP gather buffer.

### Duplicate check

Searched open PRs for `flashmla workspace` and `workspace memory leak`, and checked issue #51743 and its linked open PRs. The closest workspace PR, #42856, changes workspace bounds for SM120; it does not release retained views after growth. Issue #51743 concerns runtime padded-Q allocation rather than this retained-storage case. No matching lifetime fix was found.

## Test plan and results

- Added a parametrized regression to the existing sparse FlashMLA test suite for BF16, FP8, and FP8 with PCP+DCP. It checks obsolete-storage release, buffer shapes and non-overlap, locked pointer stability, and active workspace lane selection.
- Ran those three cases through a local CPU isolation harness loading the constructor/accessors from this checkout and the unchanged `WorkspaceManager` implementation, with real PyTorch storage. **All three fail before the patch and pass after it.** CUDA-dependent imports are stubbed in that harness; this is not a full-module or attention-kernel test.
- Ran the repository's pre-commit checks on both changed files, including Ruff and mypy.
- The deployed-version fix also passed four focused CPU regressions and the 64-rank GPU startup allocation check above.

Full-environment regression command:

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
  -k workspace_growth_releases_storage -v
```

That direct test invocation, model evaluation, long-context inference, and CUDA-graph replay validation are still pending. The local macOS environment lacks the required current vLLM dependencies and GPU runtime. The measured DEP64 configuration had CUDA graphs disabled.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Add Cohere2MoE Eagle3 auxiliary hidden states
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Enable Cohere2MoE target models to serve with compatible Eagle3 and DFlash
draft models by exposing the auxiliary hidden states required by the
speculator.

I ~am working on training~ have released a DFlash speculator for North-Mini-Code-1.0 and
realized that this was missing! Hopefully it helps others, ~especially when I
upload the checkpoints.~ :)

### Update: Public Checkpoints

As promised, the checkpoints are now public and there’s a turnkey runtime so this change can be exercised without a custom build.

**Weights (auxiliary draft/speculator checkpoints, Apache-2.0):**
 - DFlash: https://huggingface.co/sdougbrown/North-Mini-Code-1.0-dflash
 - DSpark: https://huggingface.co/sdougbrown/North-Mini-Code-1.0-dspark

**Runtime:** a thin overlay on official vLLM v0.27.1 carrying exactly this PR (#49819) plus PR #50937 (skip empty expert bias — required because North-Mini-Code w4a16 has an all-zero per-expert bias, causing vllm `0.27.1` to throw `AttributeError: 'RoutedExperts' object has no attribute 'w2_bias'`). 

Nothing is compiled from source; it’s two small pure-Python module overlays.
   - Repo: https://github.com/sdougbrown/north-mini-code-draft-runtime
   - Published multi-arch image: `ghcr.io/sdougbrown/north-mini-code runtime:v0.27.1-49819-50937`

**Validation:** both DFlash (K3) and DSpark (K4) serve and run speculative decoding on NVIDIA GB10. 

### Running the Draft Models

You can use the pre-built docker runtime I put togther if you like, or apply the patches from https://github.com/sdougbrown/north-mini-code-draft-runtime/tree/main/patches to a fresh `0.27.1` wheel and then serve:

```
   vllm serve sdougbrown/North-Mini-Code-1.0-dspark \
     --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
     --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
     --enable-auto-tool-choice \
     --tool-call-parser cohere_command4 \
     --tokenizer-mode cohere \
     --cohere-format cmd4 \
     --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_start_str":"<|START_THINKING|>","reasoning_end_str":"<|END_THINKING|>"}'
```

The easy docker path is:
```
   docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc host --shm-size 16g -p 8087:8000 \
     -e VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
     ghcr.io/sdougbrown/north-mini-code-runtime:v0.27.1-49819-50937 \
     sdougbrown/North-Mini-Code-1.0-dspark \
     --served-model-name north-mini-code-dspark \
     --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
     --max-model-len 32768 \
     --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
     --enable-auto-tool-choice \
     --tool-call-parser cohere_command4 \
     --tokenizer-mode cohere \
     --cohere-format cmd4 \
     --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_start_str":"<|START_THINKING|>","reasoning_end_str":"<|END_THINKING|>"}' \
     --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```
Note that by default this fetches the weights from huggingface. If that's not desired, you can get fancier. Here's an example I would use on my local machine assuming `~/Code` is the parent folder for the runtime repo, and `~/Models` is where I've downloaded the weights:

```
   # 1) Point the verifier at a local copy of the target and render a bundle:
   cd ~/Code/north-mini-code-draft-runtime
   VERIFIER_MODEL="$HOME/Models/North-Mini-Code-1.0-w4a16" \
     RUNTIME_WORK="$HOME/Models/north-deploy" \
     ./scripts/prepare-deployment-model.sh dspark
   # -> $HOME/Models/north-deploy/deploy/dspark
   #    (config.json now has verifier.name_or_path -> local path; weights are symlinks)

   # 2) Docker: mount Models at the SAME path and pass the bundle path:
   docker run --rm --gpus all --ipc host --shm-size 16g -p 8087:8000 \
     -e VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 \
     -v "$HOME/Models:$HOME/Models" \
     ghcr.io/sdougbrown/north-mini-code-runtime:v0.27.1-49819-50937 \
     "$HOME/Models/north-deploy/deploy/dspark" \
     --served-model-name north-mini-code-dspark \
     --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
     --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 \
     --enable-auto-tool-choice \
     --tool-call-parser cohere_command4 \
     --tokenizer-mode cohere \
     --cohere-format cmd4 \
     --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_start_str":"<|START_THINKING|>","reasoning_end_str":"<|END_THINKING|>"}' \
     --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

## Implementation

- implement `SupportsEagle3` for `Cohere2MoeForCausalLM`
- capture embedding and post-layer boundaries using global layer indices
- preserve Cohere2's parallel-residual behavior without adding the residual twice
- preserve baseline model outputs when auxiliary states are disabled
- preserve DFlash's `target_layer_ids -> auxiliary boundary + 1` semantics

Eagle3, DFlash, and DSpark with pipeline parallelism are already rejected by
the V1 GPU model runner. This change does not add auxiliary-state propagation
between pipeline stages.

## Duplicate-work check

PR #42078 added Cohere Eagle support, but it did not expose auxiliary hidden
states from the Cohere2MoE target. Searches of open PRs found no overlapping
implementation.

## Tests

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/model_executor/models/cohere2_moe.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_cohere2_moe_eagle.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/model_executor/test_cohere2_moe_eagle.py \
  tests/v1/spec_decode/test_dflash_causality.py -q
```

All pre-commit hooks passed. Pytest result: `15 passed`.

## Model evaluation

The original `a1cad4f67` implementation was successfully exercised with:

- AMD ROCm 7.2.4, TP=2, INT4/AutoGPTQ
- NVIDIA GB10 CUDA 13, TP=1, W4A16 with MARLIN NVFP4 MoE
- NVIDIA GB10 CUDA 13, TP=1, FP8 with TRITON FP8 MoE

All three configurations completed target-model requests while exposing five
finite auxiliary hidden states. The ROCm TP=2 run also verified byte-identical
per-layer values across both ranks. These runs validated the target-side
auxiliary-state path rather than end-to-end draft-token acceptance.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to port and test this change. I manually reviewed every
changed line and the test results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][HiSparse][NIXL] Import full blocks without tail prefill on D
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

HiSparse currently rejects host imports whose computed-token count is not block aligned. This draft explores an alternative to #56946: receive the full final block and restore its contents into one writable GPU page, so a successful NIXL full-prompt import resumes with a single-token forward instead of prefilling the unaligned tail on D.

The idea is that we want to avoid having to run prefill on D, however short they might be (<block_size here), with north star being deploying D with decode-only CG (aligned with rest of cases).

### NIXL analogy: transfer capacity is not sequence length

NIXL already transfers physical blocks containing partially filled prompt tails. Moving the unused bytes does not make them computed tokens. HiSparse can use the same distinction:

| For a 32,019-token prompt, block size 128 | This approach |
| --- | --- |
| Real imported tokens | 32,019 |
| Host blocks received | 251 |
| Physical capacity | 32,128 token slots |
| Unused tail capacity ("holes") | 109 token slots |
| Prompt work on D after a full import | The usual last-token replay for logits |

The holes are unused rows within the request's final host block. They do not change token positions or sequence length, and generation fills them at their normal offsets. P does not compute dummy padding tokens. No sub-block allocator or NIXL wire-protocol change is required.

### Implementation and tradeoff

- Reserve one writable resident page for the final imported block, including aligned prompts whose last token is replayed.
- After a successful external receive, enqueue a full-page host-to-device restore on every TP rank. Copies run on the compute stream before the forward/CUDA-graph replay.
- Retain both endpoints until every participating worker completes its copy. Avoid publishing an uninitialized resident copy to prefix-cache users, and keep an incomplete host page unsealed.
- Register a completed, valid restored GPU page for later prefix hits only after all workers finish. Pending restores remain hidden, and incomplete pages and aborted requests are excluded. This incorporates [NickLucche/vllm#12](https://github.com/NickLucche/vllm/pull/12).
- Continue using the existing row-mirror and page-sealing paths for newly generated KV.

Compared with #56946, this transfers the final block and pays for one page of H2D copying per layer/rank rather than recomputing up to `block_size - 1` prompt tokens. It also reserves a resident tail page for aligned imports. The unused host rows are ordinary tail capacity, not extra logical tokens or permanent gaps between prompt and output. No performance improvement has been measured.

The intended benefit is to keep successful full-prompt P/D handoffs on single-token execution, compatible with decode-only graph capture. This is not a guarantee that D can never prefill: cache misses, failed transfers, preemption, or partial external hits can still require recomputation.

### Related work

Checked #56699 and its comments, open PRs mentioning it, and open PRs matching HiSparse import, landing, tail, partial, full block, and tail restore.

- #56946 addresses the same admission failure by rounding the imported prefix down and prefilling the remainder locally. This draft is the explicitly requested alternative that retains all real prompt KV and changes tail residency instead.
- The notify-only read and empty-region shape fixes are reused verbatim from #56946 (originally #55398). They prevent empty local destinations from entering region expansion when P and D have different cache-group layouts. They are independent of tail policy; empty receives notify P, and report `finished_recving` only when `awaiting_kvs=True`.
- #55398 chooses direct GPU landing for imported history when capacity permits. This draft preserves host landing and restores only the final page.
- #56109 concerns broader pool/residency management. This draft uses the current pool model.

Related to the deployment discussion in #56699; this does not claim to fix that issue's CUDA launch failure or establish end-to-end P/D correctness.

## Test Plan

Exercise aligned, unaligned, and sub-block imports; last-token resumption; partial-page publication; multi-worker completion and abort lifetime; and tail-copy contents on both host-writer and non-writer ranks.

Before marking ready, run real NIXL P/D on NVIDIA GPUs with decode-only graphs, check generated-token/logprob parity against the prefiller reference, and exercise page-boundary crossing, eviction/preemption, and concurrent traffic. Heterogeneous TP/DCP coverage remains pending.

## Test Result

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_hisparse_connector.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py \
  -k 'hisparse or connector_completes_partial_prefix' -q
```

**99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected** on macOS. The two skipped cases require CUDA. Commit-time pre-commit hooks passed, including the configured mypy hook.

Rerun after integrating #12 and rebasing onto `upstream/main` at `fc8132a5e5`: **99 passed, 2 skipped, 117 deselected**. The existing import test now checks that one worker completion does not publish the GPU copy and that full completion publishes aligned tails. Pre-commit hooks passed across all PR files. GPU/model validation of the combined change remains pending.

Additional existing empty-receive checks after restoring those two NIXL hunks:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k empty_recv_is_reported_only_when_awaited -q
```

**4 passed, 130 deselected** on macOS. The separate completion-time positional group-pairing workaround reported by the GPU investigation is not included in this draft.

After rebasing onto `upstream/main` (`c6fa1f05d1`, including #57027), fixed the H200 CI failure in `test_hisparse_spill_and_prefix_restore[offload]`: the sync checker reports the tail copy as potentially synchronous because PyTorch does not recognize the host pool's external `cudaHostRegister` registration. A narrow `gpu_sync_allowed()` scope covers that copy; the transfer and stream ordering are unchanged. The existing CUDA tail-restore test now allocates the host pool through the production registration path and enables strict sync checking.

  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k hisparse -q

commits.pr_title: [DSv4.1] Integrate Mega-Gate from DeepGEMM
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Integrate DeepGEMM Mega-Gate into the DeepSeek V4/V4.1 DeepGEMM MegaMoE path, fusing the gate GEMM and expert selection. Prepare routing metadata once per model forward and reuse it across layers. Preserve hash routing for V4, image routing bias for V4.1, draft-layer expert counts, MTP warmup, and decoder auxiliary-state capture.

Two integration fixes are included:

- Let CMake FetchContent update an existing DeepGEMM checkout when its pinned revision changes. Previously, finding `csrc/python_api.cpp` skipped the update entirely and could rebuild 2.6.1 without `bf16_mega_gate` despite the new pin.
- ~~Clear padded hidden-state rows in place before Mega-Gate. NaN padding can trigger the kernel's finite-score assertion, later surfacing as a CUDA launch failure or NCCL error. `masked_fill_` avoids allocating a separate hidden-state tensor; valid rows are unchanged. Regression cases cover NaN padding for both main/draft and text/image routing.~~ Removed, fixed by https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/11

Update (17 Sep 2026)
- Since Mega-Gate underperforms for M<=16 (as LL-GEMM is very efficient), we only dispatch Mega-Gate for M>16

## Accuracy: full GSM8K

The final in-place implementation was evaluated locally through Vigil on **4× GB200**, using real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` weights, the current repository checkout, CUDA 13.1, and PyTorch 2.13.0. No engine overrides beyond TP4, EP, and the MegaMoE backend were supplied; CUDA Graphs remained enabled.

| Metric | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Questions | 1319 |
| Correct | **1194** |
| Accuracy | **90.5231%** |
| Invalid responses | **0** |
| API failures | **0** |
| Worker errors | **0** |
| Evaluation time | 161.79 s |


## Kernel benchmark: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Gate

Measured on a **single NVIDIA GB300 (SM103)** with BF16 inputs `[M, 5120]`, BF16 gate weights `[384, 5120]`, **top-k=6**, `sqrtsoftplus`, normalization, and routed scaling factor **1.5**. **M is the number of token rows processed on one GPU**, not serving request concurrency.

The baseline is `GateLinear + fused_topk_bias`, using its normal shape-dependent dispatch. Mega-Gate fuses the gate GEMM and expert selection. The updated DeepGEMM pin allows non-finite padding scores, eliminating the separate hidden-state padding clear; existing input staging discards padded routes.

**Mega-Gate achieves 1.18–1.31× routing speedup for M ≥ 32, with no meaningful speedup for M ≤ 16.** Speedup is baseline latency divided by Mega-Gate latency.

| Tokens M | GateLinear + top-k (μs) | Mega-Gate (μs) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 6.640 | 8.096 | 0.820× |
| 2 | 6.848 | 8.032 | 0.853× |

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Metrics] Do not log a 0.0% prefix cache hit rate before any query
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`CachingMetrics.hit_rate` returns `0.0` when `aggregated_query_total` is zero, so it cannot distinguish *no queries observed yet* from *every query missed*.

The two other cache metrics in the same log line already guard on `empty` for exactly that reason — `connector_prefix_caching_metrics` and `mm_caching_metrics` are both wrapped in `if not ...empty:`.

The main prefix cache part did not, so a server that has not yet served a prefix-cacheable request logs `Prefix cache hit rate: 0.0%`, which reads as *the cache is missing everything* rather than *nothing has been asked of it yet*.

Conditional parts are the established pattern in this log line — `Deferred` and `Preemptions` are already omitted when their counters are zero — so this makes the prefix cache consistent with its two siblings and with the rest of the line.

**Scope is the human-readable log only.** The Prometheus surface exposes `vllm:prefix_cache_queries` and `vllm:prefix_cache_hits` as raw counters, so dashboards can already separate the two cases and are unaffected.

I checked that nothing depends on the log text: no test or tool matches on it, and the existing `"MM cache hit rate"` assertions cover the sibling metric, which is already guarded.

## Test Plan

One test added beside the existing `test_metrics` in `tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py`, reusing its `_stats` helper:

    pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k metrics

`test_metrics_empty_distinguishes_no_queries_from_no_hits` asserts that `hit_rate` reads `0.0` both before any observation and after a genuine all-miss window, and that only `empty` separates them — the property the log guard depends on.

## Test Result

The arithmetic was verified against the accumulation logic in `CachingMetrics.observe`: `empty` tracks `aggregated_requests`, which `observe` increments alongside `aggregated_query_total`, so it is true exactly when `hit_rate` would return the placeholder zero.

I do not have a GPU environment to hand, so I could not run the suite locally — the test file imports torch through the package. The change is confined to log assembly and one new test, but happy to run whatever you would like to see.

If you would rather keep the line unconditionally present for log-format stability, that is a reasonable call and I am happy to close this.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Max-load throughput cliff when `max_num_seqs` is not a multiple of 8
commits.pr_body:
## Why

By default, cudagraphs are captured in (mostly) multiples of 8. When `max_num_seqs` is not set to a multiple of 8, it has the unfortunate side effect that the last bucket of batch sizes doesn't fall into a FULL cuda graph. For example, with `max_num_seqs=100` (and no spec decode), we get:

| Num decodes | Cudagraph mode |
|---|---:|
| 95 | FULL |
| 96 | FULL |
| 97 | PIECEWISE |
| 98 | PIECEWISE |
| 99 | PIECEWISE |
| 100 | PIECEWISE |

This is quite bad practically, because servers can get stuck in the slow PIECEWISE mode when it's overloaded (num_running_reqs = max_num_seqs).

In a TP4/B200 reproduction this was not a small boundary effect: batch 97 started behind batch 96 and progressively slowed over a 2,000-token decode, eventually falling below 1,000 tok/s/server. Adding the legal FULL-100 shape removed the cliff.

## Fix

This is actually already correctly handled when spec decode is turned on by #50488, but not when spec dec is off. The fix is to simply piggy-back off the PR's changes: when the inferred default is used without speculative decoding, add `max_num_seqs` as the widest uniform-decode shape if it fits under the existing capture ceiling:

```python
elif max_num_seqs <= max_cudagraph_capture_size:
    uniform_decode_sizes = [max_num_seqs]
```

For the example above, the ladder becomes:

```text
..., 88, 96, 100, 104, 112, ...
```

The unchanged graph manager then produces FULL descriptors through 100, while later sizes remain PIECEWISE-only.

## Benchmark evidence

The reproducer used [Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603](https://huggingface.co/mistralai/Mistral-Small-4-119B-2603) with TP4 on B200, `max_num_seqs=100`, logprobs enabled, 2,000 generated tokens, and a production-shaped prompt distribution with roughly equal mass around 8k, 16k, 32k, 64k, and 127k input tokens.

| Batch | Before | With FULL 100 |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 96 | 3,753 tok/s | 3,760.78 tok/s |
| 97 | 1,523 tok/s | **3,876.85 tok/s** |

Batch 97 improved 2.55× (+154.6%) and became comparable to batch 96. Before the fix its server-throughput windows decayed from 2,922 tok/s near output token 302 to 829 tok/s in the final window. After the fix they stayed flat at 3,923, 3,890, 3,862, and 3,824 tok/s. Total time fell from 129.72 s to 52.41 s.

An Nsight trace showed that the PIECEWISE path accumulated tensor-parallel rank drift: attention remained around 0.58 ms, while graph-launch gaps grew from about 0.69 ms to 5.5 ms and MNNVL all-reduce wait medians grew from about 10 µs to 3.6–4.7 ms. This PR avoids that path for a legal decode batch; it does not attempt to independently repair PIECEWISE rank drift.

## Test results

```text
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/test_config.py \
  -k default_cudagraph_capture_size_respects_platform_ceiling
11 passed, 61 deselected

VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py \
  -k 'uniform_decode_pads_up_to_full_graph or uniform_decode_exact_match_is_not_over_padded or uniform_decode_beyond_capture_ladder_falls_back or divisor_query_len_dispatch_is_unchanged'
6 passed, 5 deselected

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/config/vllm.py tests/compile/test_config.py
all hooks passed, including Ruff, mypy, SPDX, and repository checks
```

Revert check: with the production hunk reverted while retaining the new test, both cases fail (`2 failed`): neither 100 nor 101 is present in the inferred capture sizes.

No model evaluation was run because this changes only which execution graph serves an already-valid shape; model operations and outputs are unchanged.

## Not a duplicate

I searched open PRs for `max_num_seqs`, `cudagraph`, `capture sizes`, `off-stride`, and `uniform decode`. The nearby work addresses different contracts:

- #50488 introduced `uniform_decode_sizes` for speculative decoding and deliberately kept non-speculative defaults unchanged. This PR closes that remaining non-speculative boundary hole using its abstraction.
- #37865 appends `max_cudagraph_capture_size`; here that value is 200, so it still does not add the required 100-request boundary.
- #55004 covers uniform decode under an explicitly configured scalar maximum, primarily with speculative decoding. This PR changes only the inferred default and leaves explicit configuration untouched.
- #53407 lets a uniform decode pad to a wider compatible FULL graph, but it requires such a graph to exist. In this case 104 requests exceeds the scheduler limit, so there is no compatible FULL graph until 100 is captured.
- #56136 concerns candidate ladders for multiple dynamic-speculation query lengths, not the non-speculative capture set.
- #54352 is a draft auto-revert for the memory regression caused when #50488 raised capture ceilings. This patch never raises the ceiling and adds only a shape already below it.

No open PR covers an off-stride, non-speculative `max_num_seqs` boundary.

## Reviewer guide

- `vllm/config/vllm.py`: the two-line behavior change reuses the uniform-decode capture-size path; the nearby comment is updated to match its broadened scope.
- `tests/compile/test_config.py`: one new parameter exercises the existing capture-boundary contract at `max_num_seqs=100`.

There are no moves, generated files, or mechanical propagation changes.

## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, patch, tests, duplicate-work audit, and PR write-up. I reviewed every changed line and the benchmark evidence before submission.

try:

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Fix Entrypoints Integration (Pooling) tests on TheRock image
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose
`tests/entrypoints/pooling/scoring/test_cross_encoder_online_vision.py` has a number of [failures on TheRock image](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13085/list?sid=01a0ae47-79de-4154-ad16-daf19cd84150&tab=output).

This was root-caused to a slight difference in codegen on Triton 3.8 vs Triton 3.7: namely, `chunked_prefill_paged_decode`'s `_fwd_kernel` has a slightly different FP32 accumulation order which leads to a 1-ULP BF16 divergence out of 32768 elements in layer 3 given identical inputs; this 1-ULP divergence is enough to snowball over the succeeding 20+ layers.
It is important to note that both codegens are equally correct: the problematic value sits 0.034 ULP from a BF16 rounding boundary, and both codegens' values have the same max error vs a FP64 reference.

Fundamentally, the issue is that this test's golden values were designed for CUDA in #33060. ROCm's attention backends cannot reasonably be expected to have exactly the same numerics as CUDA, and indeed there have been 3 rounds of tolerance relaxation (#41341, #46891, #53646) in an attempt to reconcile the slightly different (yet still correct) numerics of ROCm's attention backends vs CUDA's golden values.
In particular, FlexAttention differs from the other backends in that it accumulates `P = softmax(QK^T)` in `Q.dtype` (which can be BF16/FP16 rather than FP32 used on all other backends on ROCm/CUDA), so it naturally has more numerical divergence.
Rather than adding yet more attention-backend-specific tolerances, the proper fix is to establish a ROCm-specific set of golden values tuned for its attention backends, which also allows the use of a unified set of `atol` and `rtol` rather than the current fragmented regime.

## Test Plan
AMD CI (in particular the `Entrypoints Integration (Pooling)` test group) was run on both [ROCm 10](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13103) and [ROCm 7.2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13108/list), on both MI300X and MI355X.

## Test Result
The test group now passes (on ROCm 10) and there are no new regressions (on ROCm 7.2).

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][CI] Adapt MoE tests to the triton_kernels 3.8 API
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

#55934 bumped `ROCM_TRITON_KERNELS_COMMIT` in `Dockerfile.rock` to the `3.8.x` branch. The library code was updated to dispatch on `get_triton_kernels_version()`, but the two MoE test modules were not, and fail against 3.8 in four ways:

  - `matmul_ogs` -> `matmul` and `matmul_ogs_details` -> `matmul_details`, imported at module scope, so collection dies with `ModuleNotFoundError` and takes out every `MoE Kernels` shard on MI300 and MI355.
  - `PrecisionConfig.weight_scale` -> `b_mx_scale`/`b_microblock_size`; 3.8 rejects the old keyword outright.
  - `make_default_matmul_mxfp4_w_layout` and its scale counterpart return a `layout` instance rather than a `(layout, opts)` pair, so unpacking raises `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable StridedLayout object`.
  - gather/scatter indices are plain tensors, so `.src_indx`/`.dst_indx` raise `AttributeError`.

## Fixes
- Dispatch the imports on `get_triton_kernels_version()`, exactly as `config.py`, `oracle/mxfp4.py` and `mxfp4_utils.py` already do.
- Route the `PrecisionConfig` weight-scale kwargs through a shared helper: `_mx_scale_kwargs` is promoted from `oracle/mxfp4.py` to a public mx_scale_kwargs` in `mxfp4_utils.py`, beside its existing read-side twin `weight_mx_scale`, so the tests are not reaching into a private helper. `oracle/mxfp4.py` imports it under the old private name, leaving its six call sites untouched.
- Add `mxfp4_w_layouts()` to the MoE tests' own `utils.py` and use it from both modules, so the layout dispatch lives in one place rather than being duplicated.
- Skip `test_routing_data_from_sparse_topk_parity` on 3.8. There `routing_data_from_sparse_topk` simply forwards to `make_routing_data`, so the test would be vacuously comparing a function against itself. This mirrors the existing 3.5.1 skip.


## Test Plan
AMD CI is run against this PR on both [ROCm 7.2](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13107) and [ROCm 10](https://buildkite.com/vllm/amd-ci/builds/13103), paying attention to the previously failing `MoE Kernels` test groups on both MI300X and MI355X and the MI355X `FP8 MoE Kernels` test group.
